I was a paratrooper not too long ago. It's a little different in that a static line connected to the plane pulls your chute open, so there's no free fall time. Being on the loud plane, feeling the Gs pull you down while you go through turbulence was the scariest part. Once I got out of the plane all that anxiety just slips away.

I do miss it

An important thing to remember about airplanes is that the spinning end hurts.

You're so jazzed when you get to the point where you're hanging off the strut that when the instructor yells GO you actually fucking do it. True story.
What if you don't? Does the instructor at one point take over control and just jump with you usually? I guess I can ask him/her before, but I'm curious about it right now.

Unless you're doing a tandem jump with the JI then your first jump is generally a static line sort of thing, where the JI holds onto the drag chute so that your chute starts deploying as soon as you let go. If you freeze up on the strut then I suppose the JI talks/pulls you back in. They can't leave you out there afterall.

The absolute most terrifying part of my first jump was when they threw the door open. The cabin was suddenly filled with wind and noise and it scared me shitless. After I calmed down from that getting out on the strut was no big thing actually.

You'll have a great time. The training beforehand is intensive (or at least it should be) and goes a long way to taking some of that uncertainly away when you make your first jump.
